targets.title: Obedience To Authority: An Experimental View
targets.evidence_quote: The obedience observed among individuals tested in Bridgeport was found to be slightly lower (48%) than that of participants tested in the Department of Psychology at Yale University (65%). Notably, even under these conditions, nearly half of the individuals exhibited complete obedience. In our study, we aimed to replicate this finding to determine whether relocating the research from a university setting to a space not associated with academic research would reduce participant obedience.
targets.outcome_quote: Therefore, this “modern” replication further confirms the enduring and universal nature of the phenomena first observed by Milgram 6 .
targets.outcome_reasoning: Authors explicitly characterize their modern replication as confirming Milgram. Location/purpose comparisons yield no differences and are discussed with ethical and power caveats; no explicit overall failure or uninformative verdict is given.

reasoning: New sample re-tests Milgram with modern equipment and recruitment and prestige manipulation. The specific primary account cited for Experiments 2 and 10 is Milgram (1974). Burger and earlier Dolinski replications provide the ethical procedure and background, without being independent targets. The 1963/1965 articles introduce the research history; the operational targets are identified through the 1974 account.
